textbookText: Sources of water pollution are discussed under following headings: i. Domestic sewage: Everything that passes from houses or residential area such as food residue, waste water after washing utensils and clothes by detergents, human excreta, animal wastes, wastes from slaughter house, and wastes from food processing industries are discharged into river, lakes, streams and other water bodies. Contents of domestic sewage are mostly biodegradable. Raw sewage contains inorganic and organic compounds and a number of pathogens causing water borne disease. Inorganic compounds are nitrate, phosphate, sodium, calcium etc. ii. Industrial effluents Waste water discharged from all industries is called effluents. Industrial wastes consists of inorganic substances such as lead, mercury, phosphorus, sulphites, sulphides etc. and organic wastes are oils, grease, organic solvents etc. some industries also use microorganisms like viruses and bacteria. These are all discharged to water bodies with water. iii. Run- off water from agriculture land Nowadays, there is competition among farmers to use different types of insecticides, pesticides, fungicides and chemical fertilizers in the name of more yields. Such chemicals decompose or degrade in nature very slowly. They are washed by rain water and mixed into river, lakes, ponds etc. altering the water quality. iv. Accidental oil spill or leakage Spilling and leakage of oil from tankers, pipelines pollute water sources. Oil is immiscible in water and thus makes a thin layer over water surface preventing aeration of water. Such condition badly affects aquatic life. v. Nuclear power plant Nuclear weapon investigation, nuclear power houses, dumping of radioactive waste and nuclear calamities are also the major source of contamination of water bodies. Mining activities of radioactive elements like uranium pollute surface water and ground water.
2. EFFECTS a. Polluted water contains pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhii causing

several waterborne diseases and bring epidemic condition in the community. b. When organic compounds or wastes exceed optimum level in water, decaying of such wastes needs large number of decomposers or microorganisms. These microorganisms need large amount of oxygen for decomposition of these organic wastes, leading to the rise of BOD or biological oxygen demand. BOD is defined as the amount of oxygen required by micro-organism while oxidizing the entire organic matter present in one litre of water at given temperature. Value of BOD is more in polluted water. c. Waste water discharged from most of the industries may be at higher temperature. Electric power plant, nuclear power station and thermal power plant use water as coolant and these units release hot water to nearby sources like river, sea and lake Biology, Grade 11 | 463

raising temperature of these water bodies. It is also called thermal pollution. Such activity causes the oxygen depletion in water and threats aquatic life. d. Pesticides and fertilizers after being swept or washed away by rain water mix to nearby water sources and alter the overall chemical composition of water which affects freshwater and marine ecosystem. These substances may incorporate into food chain and get accumulated in organisms of higher trophic level. e. Nuclear power plants established in the coastal regions emit radiations and atomic wastes which pollute water and bring several health hazards to marine animals and human beings who consume seafood. f. Water bodies become enriched or overloaded by nutrients such as phosphate and nitrates found in domestic sewage, industrial effluents and run off from field. Consequently, growth of more aquatic plants and algal bloom take place in water. This prevents aeration of water and entry of sunlight. Death and decay of these algal blooms need more decomposer and bacteria which demand more oxygen in water and the entire condition is called Eutrophication. g. Some metals such as Mercury, lead etc. in polluted water bring serious health related issues like cancer, renal disorder, eyes problem, nervous and cardiovascular disorder, skin allergies etc.

3. PREVENTIVE MEASURES i. Household degradable organic wastes and sewage can be collected and converted to compost manure. ii. Industrial effluents should be treated and made least toxic before discharging into water sources. iii. If possible wastes can be recycled or treated before dumped. iv. Use of insecticide, pesticide and fertilizer (agrochemicals) should be banned in agriculture field. v. Making people aware, afforestation, checking population growth and strict implementation of environment protection act are main ways to prevent water pollution.
